title: HCP — Delegation
description: The Human Context Protocol (HCP) 2.0-draft-3 delegation (Delegated Authorization Profile, HCP 17.2), shared by the hcp/* tasks. Written for this registry from the HCP 2.0-draft-3 specification text (CC BY 4.0, https://github.com/loyalagents/hcp-spec), with attribution, and checked against the shapes HCP publishes for the same draft; not copied from HCP's own schema files. Open, as HCP's own shapes are. Where this schema and the HCP text differ, the HCP text governs. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty, which an hcp/* party never writes empty. hcp/import applies neither to an export it takes.

Delegation.description: One natural person's authority to act as Authorizing Principal for the Context Subject (HCP 17.2). The Authorization Service establishes it and the provider holds its record; neither the Context Subject nor the delegate may change it, and a change is a new delegation (HCP 17.2).

delegationId.description: Stable for the life of the delegation; named by every grant issued under it and by audit events (HCP 17.2).

delegate.description: The delegate: a natural person, with a name the Context Subject can recognize (HCP 17.1, 17.2).

name.description: A name the Context Subject can recognize.

relationship.description: The delegate's relationship to the Context Subject: a value registered in HCP A.1 (`parent-or-guardian`, `legal-guardian`, `attorney-in-fact`, `caregiver`) or an absolute URI. It confers nothing by itself; `scope` sets what the delegate may do (HCP 17.2). Distinct from an entry's reserved `subject.relationship` (HCP 11.3). The pattern admits the slug or an absolute URI's outline only: it carries no `format: uri`, which would refuse every slug, so checking that a custom value is a well-formed absolute URI, as HCP's prose requires (HCP A.3), is the consumer's check.

basis.description: What the authority rests on, and how the Authorization Service established it (HCP 17.3).

scope.description: The categories and actions the delegate may authorize (HCP 17.4).

mayDelegate.description: True where the delegate may appoint a sub-delegate (HCP 17.10). Absent means false. Recorded by the Authorization Service (HCP 17.2).

ended.description: Absent while the delegation holds; set when it ends, with the reason (HCP 17.6).

DelegationBasis.description: What a delegation's authority rests on (HCP 17.3). Where `method` is `evidence`, `evidence` is present with at least one item; `parent` is present exactly where `method` is `delegated` (HCP 17.3, 17.10). Those rules are not checked by the schema: the registry's Rust generator does not support `if`/`then`/`else`, so a validator does not check them.

method.description: How the authority was established (HCP 17.3). `unspecified` is used only for a delegation converted from HCP v1 and MUST NOT be presented to anyone as `attested` (HCP 17.3, 17.8).

description.description: What the authority rests on, shown to the Context Subject and the delegate (HCP 17.3). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

parent.description: For a sub-delegation (`method` `delegated`), the delegation it came from (HCP 17.10).

evidence.description: The evidence presented, for `method` `evidence`: a credential of guardianship, a court order, a power of attorney. A Verifiable Credential is held whole, as an entry's evidence item is (HCP 17.3, 4.2.2). The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

covers.description: The High-sensitivity and custom categories the basis extends to; only these may be in `scope` (HCP 17.4). The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

establishedBy.description: The Authorization Service that established the delegation (HCP 17.2).

DelegationScope.description: The categories and actions a delegate may authorize; every category is named, with no wildcard (HCP 17.4).

categories.description: The categories in scope (HCP 17.4). The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

DelegationTerm.description: When a delegation ends: at `endsAt`, and at the Context Subject's age of majority where `atMajority` is true (HCP 17.2).

endsAt.description: When the delegation ends; null where no end is known (HCP 17.2).

atMajority.description: True where the delegation ends at the Context Subject's age of majority, which the Authorization Service determines under the law that applies (HCP 17.2).

DelegationEnded.description: How and when a delegation ended (HCP 17.6). The member name `at` is HCP's own, carried verbatim.

reason.description: Why it ended (HCP 17.6). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.
